title: The depth of a module is at most dim(R/p) for every associated prime p
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal for which there is an element $z\in M$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\{a\in R: az=0\}=\mathfrak p$ (an associated prime of $M$). Then $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)$, where $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$ is the Krull dimension of the ring $R/\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth].
